tldr: Wild Salmon Center submitted a comment to Oregon's Prosperity Council (June 1, 2026) urging integration of natural resource protection into the state's economic strategy. They argue healthy ecosystems—including forests, water, salmon, and outdoor recreation—are foundational to economic growth. They cite $16B in outdoor recreation spending (2022), $642M in commercial fisheries (2021), and demonstrate that habitat restoration generates significant local jobs and economic activity, calling for alignment with Governor's Executive Order 25-26.

bullets.text: Commercial fisheries in Oregon generated $642 million in 2021 alone
Outdoor recreation in Oregon supported $16 billion in spending and 192,000 full or part-time jobs in 2022
Fishing, hunting, and wildlife viewing contributed $1.2 billion in spending and supported 11,000 jobs, generating $385 million in labor income
Oregon Coast captured 17% ($2.053 billion) of total statewide spending and 59% (17 million) of all visitors to Oregon in 2018
Between 2001 and 2010, habitat restoration in Oregon generated up to 6,400 jobs and more than $977 million in economic activity
Every $1 million invested in watershed restoration results in an average of 16 to 17 new jobs and $2.3 million in economic activity
80 percent of Oregon Watershed Enhancement Board grant funding remains in the county where the project is located
53% of Oregonians believe that maintaining a quality environment attracts people and companies to Oregon

bureaus: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
